feat(windows): auto-update via Velopack C++ SDK + query result column resize

- Vendor Velopack C++ SDK 0.0.1298 (Velopack.hpp header + x64 static lib)
- UpdateService wraps UpdateManager with async check + download/apply
  against R2 feed at https://cdn.gridex.app/windows/
- App::App() runs VelopackApp::Build().Run() to handle installer hooks
- MainWindow shows an UpdateCheckOverlay at startup, blocks entry to
  HomePage until the check resolves; an update dialog offers Install
  (applies delta + restarts) or Later (enters the app)
- Settings page adds a manual "Check Now" button for on-demand checks
- QueryEditorView result grid gets drag-to-resize column headers,
  mirroring the DataGridView pattern

Also remove the GitHub Actions Windows Release workflow — free tier
Actions minutes run out; Setup.exe is now uploaded manually to R2 and
GitHub Releases from a local pack run.

fix(windows): bundle d2.exe v0.7.1 for ER Diagram rendering

ER Diagram feature shells out to Assets/d2/d2.exe to render the schema
into SVG. Previously only LICENSE + README.txt lived in Assets/d2/, so
the 0.0.5 installer shipped without the binary and users saw:

  Failed: d2.exe not found. Place it in Assets\d2\d2.exe.

Vendor the D2 CLI (Windows amd64, 48 MB) next to its existing LICENSE
and override the repo-wide *.exe ignore for that single path so future
builds + packages pick it up automatically.

fix(windows): new-row insert + auto-flush inline cell edit

- ChangeTracker.generateInsert now omits columns with blank values so
  AUTO_INCREMENT / SERIAL / column DEFAULT fire. Previously emitted
  '' for every blank cell, which MySQL rejected on INT columns and
  which also blocked auto-increment from running. Same fix applied
  defensively to MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQLite/MSSQL adapter insertRow.
  All-blank rows now use each dialect's DEFAULT VALUES form.
- DataGridView.FlushEdit(): locate the active edit TextBox and
  commit its text synchronously. Called at the top of
  WorkspacePage.CommitChanges so Ctrl+S no longer loses the typed
  value (accelerator didn't move focus, LostFocus never fired, SQL
  used the pre-edit value — often NULL for new rows).
- Grid-level PointerPressed handler flushes when the click lands
  outside the active TextBox, so clicking another row or the empty
  area also confirms the edit. Clicks inside the TextBox skip flush
  so caret repositioning still works.

fix(windows): MySQL connection on external servers + surface real error

Two things were fighting to prevent Windows users from connecting to
external MySQL servers that macOS (MySQLNIO) connected to fine.

1. libmariadb 3.4 (vcpkg) restricts auth plugins by default to a
   whitelist that does NOT include mysql_native_password — the most
   common server-side auth plugin. Handshake bombed with
   'Authentication plugin mysql_native_password couldn't be found in
   restricted_auth plugin list'. Explicit whitelist added covering
   every real plugin (native/sha2/ed25519/gssapi/dialog/etc).

2. libmariadb 3.4 also auto-upgrades the connection to TLS whenever
   the server advertises CLIENT_SSL and defaults verify_server_cert
   to TRUE. Users who picked 'Disabled' SSL got TLS anyway, then
   'Certificate verification failure: The certificate is NOT trusted'
   against a self-signed cert. Fix: always pin verify_server_cert to
   0 unless the user explicitly chose VerifyCA / VerifyIdentity.
   Disabled / Preferred / Required now never fail on cert trust.

Also added ConnectionManager::testConnectionWithError so the UI can
display the driver's real message instead of the generic 'check host,
port, credentials' line; HomePage uses it on both new-connection save
and existing-connection open.

fix(windows): preserve pending-delete red mark across selection changes

Only the most recently deleted row kept its red background — deleting
a second row stripped the first one of its mark, because HighlightRow
reset the previous selection's background without knowing the row was
still pending deletion. ChangeTracker was unaffected so commit still
issued all DELETEs correctly, but the UI lied.

DataGridView now owns a std::set<int> deletedRows_ that MarkRowDeleted
writes to and ClearRowMarks / SetData clear. HighlightRow checks the
set first and paints red + Opacity(0.5) regardless of selection state,
so pending deletes survive any number of selection changes.

fix(windows): bundle libmariadb auth plugin DLLs + set plugin dir at runtime

The only built-in auth plugin in libmariadb is mysql_native_password —
everything else (caching_sha2_password, client_ed25519, sha256_password,
dialog, mysql_clear_password) ships as a separate DLL loaded from
MYSQL_PLUGIN_DIR. Gridex wasn't shipping those DLLs, and libmariadb's
default plugin dir points to a compile-time vcpkg path that doesn't
exist on customer machines. Result: anyone whose MySQL server used the
default auth (MySQL 8 → caching_sha2_password, MariaDB 10.4+ →
client_ed25519) couldn't connect, only people running MySQL with an
explicit --default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password could.

Fix is two-part:
- build-unpackaged.ps1 copies every libmariadb plugin DLL from
  C:\vcpkg\installed\x64-windows\plugins\libmariadb\ to
  <app>\plugins\mariadb- MySQLAdapter.cpp computes <exe_dir>\plugins\mariadb at connect
  time and hands it to mysql_options(MYSQL_PLUGIN_DIR, ...), so the
  library finds the plugins regardless of where the user installed
  Gridex.

Verified live against:
- MySQL 8.0.45 default (caching_sha2_password) ✓
- MariaDB 10.11 default (client_ed25519) ✓
- MySQL 8 with --default-auth=mysql_native_password ✓

refactor(windows): expose ERDiagramService D2 helpers as public static (#10)

Promote file-scope static helpers to public static members of
ERDiagramService so other services can reuse consistent D2 escaping,
temp-file, and d2.exe subprocess logic without copy-paste drift.

- SanitizeIdentifier / IsD2Reserved / QuoteIfReserved: D2 identifier
  rules extracted from GenerateD2Text internals.
- EscapeD2Label (new): wrap + escape a string for use as a D2 quoted
  label; handles embedded quotes, backslashes, newlines.
- TempPath: accepts an optional prefix param (default "er_" keeps
  existing behavior); counter upgraded to std::atomic<int> so distinct
  prefixes can share the filename namespace safely.
- RunD2: same signature, now a class method instead of file-scope.

Zero behavior change for existing callers — all internal call sites in
GenerateD2Text and Generate updated to use the new capitalized names.

* feat(windows): add row-relationship extension points to DataGridView + DatabaseAdapter

Opt-in extension points so downstream code (upcoming enterprise row
relationship graph feature) can hook into row right-click actions and
assemble safe SQL for the active engine without fork-patching OSS.

DataGridView
- New public callback OnViewRelationshipsRequested.
- "View Relationship" MenuFlyoutItem + separator, stays Collapsed until
  a host wires the callback (OSS builds show no item). Enabled only
  when a row is selected.
- Link glyph (\xE71B) for the icon.

DatabaseAdapter
- New virtual quoteSqlLiteral and quoteSqlIdentifier, both with a
  default impl that throws. Non-SQL adapters (Mongo, Redis) inherit
  the throw so accidental calls fail loudly instead of silently
  producing wrong SQL.
- PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite / MSSQL override both, delegating to the
  existing utf8 quoteLiteral / quoteIdentifier helpers and converting
  the result back to wstring.

Zero behavior change for existing call paths — the new virtuals are
additive API, and the DataGridView item is hidden unless opted in.

feat(mcp): add MCP server with hardened SQL write tools

Adds a Model Context Protocol server so external AI clients (Claude
  Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code) can read and modify the user's
  databases under explicit approval gates.

  Server
  - JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio transport; `--mcp-stdio` CLI entry point
  - 13 tools across 3 tiers: schema (list/describe), read (query,
    explain, search), write (insert/update/delete/raw-write)
  - Per-connection access modes (locked | read-only | read-write) with
    session-cached user approval for write operations
  - JSONL audit log, rate limiter, menu-bar status indicator

  UI
  - Dedicated MCP window (Overview / Connections / Activity / Setup /
    Config tabs) with prominent Start/Stop control and live uptime
  - One-click install of Gridex into Claude Desktop / Cursor / Windsurf
    / Claude Code config files (merges with existing mcpServers, keeps
    a .bak of the original)

  Security
  - MCPIdentifierValidator: ASCII allowlist for table / schema / column
    names received from AI clients
  - MCPSQLSanitizer: strips SQL comments and string literals before
    syntactic checks, so payloads hidden in `/* WHERE */` or `-- …` no
    longer bypass the bare-UPDATE/DELETE guard
  - validateWhereClause rejects `;`, `--`, `/*`, `*/`, tautologies
  - validateReadOnlyQuery rejects multi-statements and blocks DML/DDL
    plus side-effectful functions (NEXTVAL, DBLINK, COPY, LO_IMPORT,
    pg_read_server_files, CALL, EXEC, …)
  - Dialect-quoted identifiers in every write tool; row-count dry-run
    runs against the already-quoted qualifiedTable and never re-parses
    user SQL to reconstruct a COUNT(*) query

* feat(windows): fetch AI model list from provider API in Settings

Replaces the plain 'type the model name yourself' TextBox with an
editable ComboBox + Refresh button. Click Refresh → hit the selected
provider's listing endpoint on a worker thread → populate the dropdown
with the live list alphabetized. User's current text is preserved
across refreshes so free-typed custom names (OpenAI-compatible proxies
like DeepSeek / Groq / self-hosted endpoints) still work — ComboBox
stays IsEditable=true for exactly that case.

New AiService::FetchModels(AiConfig) — synchronous, returns success /
models / errorMessage. Handles each provider's auth + response shape:
- Anthropic: /v1/models?limit=1000, x-api-key header
- OpenAI: /v1/models, Bearer token
- Ollama: /api/tags against the user's endpoint, no auth
- Gemini: /v1beta/models?key=..., strips models/ prefix
- OpenRouter: /api/v1/models, optional Bearer

Save path unchanged (still writes aiModel as a string), so existing
settings.json files round-trip fine.

* feat(windows): render ER diagram in-process via dagre + WebView, drop d2.exe

ER Diagram no longer shells out to d2.exe for rendering. New path:
- ERDiagramService::GenerateJson walks the adapter schema and emits a
  compact JSON payload ({tables:[{name,columns:[{name,type,isPk,isFk,
  nullable}]}], edges:[{fromTable,fromColumn,toTable,toColumn}]}).
- The existing WebView2 ER tab loads bundled Assets/er-diagram/
  dagre.min.js + svg-pan-zoom.min.js and renders the cards + edges
  hand-rolled — no external process, no temp SVG file.
- erD2Text still generated (kept the old Copy D2 flow intact as an
  export affordance) but isn't on the render path anymore.

Toolbar cleanup on the ER tab: drop 'Copy D2', 'Save SVG...', 'Save
D2...'. One 'Export PNG...' button replaces them (exports what the
user actually sees in the WebView).

Why: d2.exe bundling is 40+ MB and the subprocess launch added a
noticeable pause on first render; the JS renderer starts instantly
and handles pan/zoom natively through svg-pan-zoom.

fix(mongodb): default authSource=admin and surface server error message (#14)

The MongoDB connection form failed with a generic "MongoServerError error 1"
  because the URI omitted authSource. MongoKitten then authenticated against
  the target database, while most users have credentials in the admin DB.

  - buildURI: append ?authSource=admin when credentials are provided
  - wrap(mongoError:): extract errmsg/codeName from MongoServerError and
    MongoGenericErrorReply so the user sees the real failure reason instead
    of NSError's default "operation couldn't be completed (… error 1.)"
  - Package.swift: expose MongoClient product (needed for the error types)

    authenticate against the admin DB instead of the target database.
  - Surface real MongoDB server error messages (errmsg/codeName) instead

fix(mcp): harden stdio reader so Claude Desktop connect never aborts

Debug popup "abort() has been called" fired from the AppX Debug
build when Claude Desktop connected to Gridex --mcp-stdio. Root
cause: an uncaught exception on the reader thread escaped the
existing std::exception-only catch block; Debug CRT turned the
resulting std::terminate into abort() + popup.

Harden every cross-thread boundary so a single malformed
request or SEH escape can never crash the whole server:

* StdioTransport::readLoop — add catch(...) fallback alongside
  the std::exception catch. Both paths try-swallow the
  follow-up `send` to a dead transport.
* MCPServer::handleRequest — wrap the dispatch switch in
  try/catch; exceptions from handleInitialize /
  handleToolsList / handleToolsCall become JSON-RPC
  internalError responses with the caught message, not a
  thread termination.
* App::OnLaunched stdio branch — wrap MCPServerHost setup in
  try/catch + ExitProcess(2) so a constructor failure (audit
  logger folder create, settings parse) surfaces cleanly
  instead of aborting before Claude sees any output.
* Temporarily flip StdioTransport::kDebug to true so future
  stdio regressions leave a trail at
  %APPDATA%\Gridex\mcp-stdio-debug.log.

fix(mcp): warn before writing AppX/Debug path to Claude config

Root cause of 'abort() has been called' popup when Claude Desktop
connected to Gridex: the Install button stamped whatever exe
path the current process had into claude_desktop_config.json.
When the user was F5-ing an MSIX Debug AppX build from Visual
Studio, that path pointed at
 E:\dev\be\gridex\windows\x64\Debug\Gridex\AppX\Gridex.exe
which Claude cannot spawn as a plain child process — MSIX needs
package activation context, and without it the CRT aborts early
at load (before OnLaunched even runs, so our stdio hardening
couldn't catch it).

Guard in MCPPage::InstallClaude_Click now inspects
GetModuleFileNameW output and refuses to write the config if
the exe sits under an 'AppX' or 'Debug' folder; the status
label directs the user at the Release build (or the
build-unpackaged.ps1 self-contained output) which is what we
tested successfully via stdio pipe in this session.

fix(mcp): stop lying about prompts/resources capabilities — Claude CLI rejects

Claude CLI handshake flow:
  initialize -> server advertises capabilities
  tools/list -> ok
  prompts/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  resources/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  -> Claude CLI marks connection failed because the server
     advertised prompts + resources in its initialize response
     but then 404'd their list endpoints. It's a spec violation
     and the mac port inherited it because the Swift
     MCPServerInfo.gridex() stamped all four capability keys
     even though only tools was wired up.

Fix:
  * MCPServerInfo::mcpDefaultCapabilities — expose tools +
    logging only. Prompts / resources land when they actually
    have handlers.
  * MCPServer::handleRequest — handle prompts/list,
    resources/list, resources/templates/list by returning
    well-formed empty lists so clients that probe them anyway
    (Claude CLI does) see a healthy server instead of a
    methodNotFound disconnect trigger.
  * Also accept `notifications/initialized` (fully-qualified
    form Claude CLI uses) as a no-response notification.

Verified via smoke pipe: initialize -> 175 B (slimmer payload),
tools/list -> 1637 B (4 tools), prompts/list -> 49 B empty,
resources/list -> 51 B empty, EOF clean.

feat(mcp): Round 1B — 4 Tier-3 write tools with approval gate

  can't abort the batch.

  sees the new rows appear in the sidebar (RefreshList now
  re-reads the store from the previous commit); a separate
  toast is redundant and was the crash trigger.

* fix(mcp): harden stdio reader so Claude Desktop connect never aborts

Debug popup "abort() has been called" fired from the AppX Debug
build when Claude Desktop connected to Gridex --mcp-stdio. Root
cause: an uncaught exception on the reader thread escaped the
existing std::exception-only catch block; Debug CRT turned the
resulting std::terminate into abort() + popup.

Harden every cross-thread boundary so a single malformed
request or SEH escape can never crash the whole server:

* StdioTransport::readLoop — add catch(...) fallback alongside
  the std::exception catch. Both paths try-swallow the
  follow-up `send` to a dead transport.
* MCPServer::handleRequest — wrap the dispatch switch in
  try/catch; exceptions from handleInitialize /
  handleToolsList / handleToolsCall become JSON-RPC
  internalError responses with the caught message, not a
  thread termination.
* App::OnLaunched stdio branch — wrap MCPServerHost setup in
  try/catch + ExitProcess(2) so a constructor failure (audit
  logger folder create, settings parse) surfaces cleanly
  instead of aborting before Claude sees any output.
* Temporarily flip StdioTransport::kDebug to true so future
  stdio regressions leave a trail at
  %APPDATA%\Gridex\mcp-stdio-debug.log.

* fix(mcp): warn before writing AppX/Debug path to Claude config

connected to Gridex: the Install button stamped whatever exe
path the current process had into claude_desktop_config.json.
When the user was F5-ing an MSIX Debug AppX build from Visual
Studio, that path pointed at

which Claude cannot spawn as a plain child process — MSIX needs
package activation context, and without it the CRT aborts early
at load (before OnLaunched even runs, so our stdio hardening
couldn't catch it).

GetModuleFileNameW output and refuses to write the config if
the exe sits under an 'AppX' or 'Debug' folder; the status
label directs the user at the Release build (or the

* fix(mcp): stop lying about prompts/resources capabilities — Claude CLI rejects

Claude CLI handshake flow:
  initialize -> server advertises capabilities
  tools/list -> ok
  prompts/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  resources/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  -> Claude CLI marks connection failed because the server
     advertised prompts + resources in its initialize response
     but then 404'd their list endpoints. It's a spec violation
     and the mac port inherited it because the Swift
     MCPServerInfo.gridex() stamped all four capability keys
     even though only tools was wired up.

Fix:
  * MCPServerInfo::mcpDefaultCapabilities — expose tools +
    logging only. Prompts / resources land when they actually
    have handlers.
  * MCPServer::handleRequest — handle prompts/list,
    resources/list, resources/templates/list by returning
    well-formed empty lists so clients that probe them anyway
    (Claude CLI does) see a healthy server instead of a
    methodNotFound disconnect trigger.
  * Also accept `notifications/initialized` (fully-qualified
    form Claude CLI uses) as a no-response notification.

Verified via smoke pipe: initialize -> 175 B (slimmer payload),
tools/list -> 1637 B (4 tools), prompts/list -> 49 B empty,
resources/list -> 51 B empty, EOF clean.

never writes to. Passwords actually live DPAPI-encrypted in the
SQLite `password_enc` column; ConnectionStore::Load decrypts them
into ConnectionConfig::password.

Read the password directly off the ConnectionConfig we already

after an import the sidebar looked unchanged until the user
closed + reopened the app (which triggered the Loaded handler
and its one-time ConnectionStore::Load).

* fix(import): scan legacy Navicat\Servers hive so "Navicat for MySQL" users get both connections

User reported 2 Navicat connections, only 1 imported. Diagnosis:
second connection lived in HKCU\Software\PremiumSoft\Navicat\
Servers\... — the plain "Navicat" hive used by the original
"Navicat for MySQL" standalone product, which my importer never
read. Only the Premium + product-specific hives (PG / MARIADB /
MSSQL / MONGODB / REDIS / SQLite / Premium) were in the scan

* fix(import): drop follow-up ContentDialog + guard CheckBox reads post-dismiss

User reported crash after Import Selected — sidebar didn't
refresh, app terminated. Two interacting issues:

1. Snapshotting CheckBox.IsChecked() AFTER `co_await op` meant
   the controls were already mid-teardown when we read them.
   WinUI 3 can throw from the getter once the dialog starts
   animating out; the throw propagated unhandled from the
   fire_and_forget coroutine and killed the process.

2. Back-to-back ContentDialogs on the same XamlRoot (import
   dialog → "Import Complete" confirmation) are historically
   fragile in WinUI 3 — even when the first has resolved, the
   second ShowAsync can throw if teardown isn't fully done.

Fix:
* Wrap the whole ShowAsync + co_await in try/catch, drop out
  on any exception.
* Snapshot selected indices into a plain vector INSIDE a
  per-checkbox try/catch, then close the dialog scope before
  touching ConnectionStore.
* Every Save() call individually try/wrapped so one bad row
  can't abort the batch.
* Remove the follow-up ContentDialog entirely. User already
  sees the new rows appear in the sidebar (RefreshList now
  re-reads the store from the previous commit); a separate
  toast is redundant and was the crash trigger.

* fix(import): buffer overflow in newConnectionId crashed import save

swprintf_s was writing 32 hex chars + null terminator into a 32-wchar
buffer. UCRT debug assertion 'Buffer too small' at output.cpp:282 fired
the moment the user clicked 'Import N Connection(s)' — newConnectionId
runs for every imported connection missing an id, and the off-by-one
took down the whole process. Bumped buffer to 33.

feat(clickhouse): add ClickHouse adapter via HTTP interface

no new SPM dependency. Supports full mTLS via PKCS#12 client bundle +
pinned CA (PEM or DER). Version-aware introspection falls back to
`system.tables.primary_key` for ClickHouse <21.3.

- `ClickHouseAdapter` conforms to `DatabaseAdapter` + `SchemaInspectable`;

- Backup/restore emits `SHOW CREATE TABLE` + `FORMAT Values` dumps

feat(clickhouse): add ClickHouse adapter via HTTP interface

Full PG-adapter parity for ClickHouse connections. Transport: HTTP
port 8123 using cpp-httplib (avoids clickhouse-cpp's abseil build

fix(clickhouse): winsock2 include order + drop SSLClient (httplib built w/o OpenSSL)

Three compile-breakers from the initial CH landing:

1. <windows.h> was included before <winsock2.h>, so the legacy
   winsock.h got dragged in first and clashed with winsock2 structs
   (sockaddr, fd_set, timeval…) — 100+ C2011 redefinition errors.
   Reordered: WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN + winsock2 + ws2tcpip first, then
   windows.h.

2. httplib::SSLClient is gated by CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT which
   the vendored build does not define. Dropped the TLS branch; plain
   httplib::Client only. Users needing TLS can front CH with
   nginx/Caddy and point us at the plaintext backend.

3. String-literal concat ('...' + '`' + db) — two pointers can't be
   added. Wrapped the first literal in std::string().

fix(clickhouse): currentSchema defaults to connected DB, drop built-in functions from sidebar

Two bugs were hiding user tables:

1. WorkspacePage default currentSchema_ = "public" (PG convention)
   had no ClickHouse branch, so listTables("public") / fetchRows
   kept looking for a non-existent public.<t>. Mirrored the MySQL
   branch — CH has no schemas, the database IS the schema.

2. listFunctions used origin='System' which returns ~1000 built-ins
   (BIT_AND, sumMap, …) and flooded the sidebar. Some sidebar paths
   even tried to open them as tables. Scoped to 'SQLUserDefined' so
   only user functions show, matching PG/MySQL behaviour.

* fix(mcp): harden stdio reader so Claude Desktop connect never aborts

Debug popup "abort() has been called" fired from the AppX Debug
build when Claude Desktop connected to Gridex --mcp-stdio. Root
cause: an uncaught exception on the reader thread escaped the
existing std::exception-only catch block; Debug CRT turned the
resulting std::terminate into abort() + popup.

Harden every cross-thread boundary so a single malformed
request or SEH escape can never crash the whole server:

* StdioTransport::readLoop — add catch(...) fallback alongside
  the std::exception catch. Both paths try-swallow the
  follow-up `send` to a dead transport.
* MCPServer::handleRequest — wrap the dispatch switch in
  try/catch; exceptions from handleInitialize /
  handleToolsList / handleToolsCall become JSON-RPC
  internalError responses with the caught message, not a
  thread termination.
* App::OnLaunched stdio branch — wrap MCPServerHost setup in
  try/catch + ExitProcess(2) so a constructor failure (audit
  logger folder create, settings parse) surfaces cleanly
  instead of aborting before Claude sees any output.
* Temporarily flip StdioTransport::kDebug to true so future
  stdio regressions leave a trail at
  %APPDATA%\Gridex\mcp-stdio-debug.log.

* fix(mcp): warn before writing AppX/Debug path to Claude config

Root cause of 'abort() has been called' popup when Claude Desktop
connected to Gridex: the Install button stamped whatever exe
path the current process had into claude_desktop_config.json.
When the user was F5-ing an MSIX Debug AppX build from Visual
Studio, that path pointed at
 E:\dev\be\gridex\windows\x64\Debug\Gridex\AppX\Gridex.exe
which Claude cannot spawn as a plain child process — MSIX needs
package activation context, and without it the CRT aborts early
at load (before OnLaunched even runs, so our stdio hardening
couldn't catch it).

Guard in MCPPage::InstallClaude_Click now inspects
GetModuleFileNameW output and refuses to write the config if
the exe sits under an 'AppX' or 'Debug' folder; the status
label directs the user at the Release build (or the
build-unpackaged.ps1 self-contained output) which is what we
tested successfully via stdio pipe in this session.

* fix(mcp): stop lying about prompts/resources capabilities — Claude CLI rejects

Claude CLI handshake flow:
  initialize -> server advertises capabilities
  tools/list -> ok
  prompts/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  resources/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  -> Claude CLI marks connection failed because the server
     advertised prompts + resources in its initialize response
     but then 404'd their list endpoints. It's a spec violation
     and the mac port inherited it because the Swift
     MCPServerInfo.gridex() stamped all four capability keys
     even though only tools was wired up.

Fix:
  * MCPServerInfo::mcpDefaultCapabilities — expose tools +
    logging only. Prompts / resources land when they actually
    have handlers.
  * MCPServer::handleRequest — handle prompts/list,
    resources/list, resources/templates/list by returning
    well-formed empty lists so clients that probe them anyway
    (Claude CLI does) see a healthy server instead of a
    methodNotFound disconnect trigger.
  * Also accept `notifications/initialized` (fully-qualified
    form Claude CLI uses) as a no-response notification.

Verified via smoke pipe: initialize -> 175 B (slimmer payload),
tools/list -> 1637 B (4 tools), prompts/list -> 49 B empty,
resources/list -> 51 B empty, EOF clean.

never writes to. Passwords actually live DPAPI-encrypted in the
SQLite `password_enc` column; ConnectionStore::Load decrypts them
into ConnectionConfig::password.

loaded. Removed the stale CredentialManager include.

"Navicat for MySQL" standalone product, which my importer never
read. Only the Premium + product-specific hives (PG / MARIADB /
MSSQL / MONGODB / REDIS / SQLite / Premium) were in the scan

* fix(import): drop follow-up ContentDialog + guard CheckBox reads post-dismiss

User reported crash after Import Selected — sidebar didn't
refresh, app terminated. Two interacting issues:

1. Snapshotting CheckBox.IsChecked() AFTER `co_await op` meant
   the controls were already mid-teardown when we read them.
   WinUI 3 can throw from the getter once the dialog starts
   animating out; the throw propagated unhandled from the
   fire_and_forget coroutine and killed the process.

2. Back-to-back ContentDialogs on the same XamlRoot (import
   dialog → "Import Complete" confirmation) are historically
   fragile in WinUI 3 — even when the first has resolved, the
   second ShowAsync can throw if teardown isn't fully done.

* Wrap the whole ShowAsync + co_await in try/catch, drop out
  on any exception.
* Snapshot selected indices into a plain vector INSIDE a
  per-checkbox try/catch, then close the dialog scope before
  touching ConnectionStore.
* Every Save() call individually try/wrapped so one bad row
  can't abort the batch.
* Remove the follow-up ContentDialog entirely. User already
  sees the new rows appear in the sidebar (RefreshList now
  re-reads the store from the previous commit); a separate
  toast is redundant and was the crash trigger.

* fix(clickhouse): winsock2 include order + drop SSLClient (httplib built w/o OpenSSL)

Three compile-breakers from the initial CH landing:

1. <windows.h> was included before <winsock2.h>, so the legacy
   winsock.h got dragged in first and clashed with winsock2 structs
   (sockaddr, fd_set, timeval…) — 100+ C2011 redefinition errors.
   Reordered: WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN + winsock2 + ws2tcpip first, then
   windows.h.

2. httplib::SSLClient is gated by CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT which
   the vendored build does not define. Dropped the TLS branch; plain
   httplib::Client only. Users needing TLS can front CH with
   nginx/Caddy and point us at the plaintext backend.

   added. Wrapped the first literal in std::string().

   kept looking for a non-existent public.<t>. Mirrored the MySQL
   branch — CH has no schemas, the database IS the schema.

2. listFunctions used origin='System' which returns ~1000 built-ins
   (BIT_AND, sumMap, …) and flooded the sidebar. Some sidebar paths
   even tried to open them as tables. Scoped to 'SQLUserDefined' so
   only user functions show, matching PG/MySQL behaviour.

Debug popup "abort() has been called" fired from the AppX Debug

cause: an uncaught exception on the reader thread escaped the
existing std::exception-only catch block; Debug CRT turned the
resulting std::terminate into abort() + popup.

Harden every cross-thread boundary so a single malformed
request or SEH escape can never crash the whole server:

* StdioTransport::readLoop — add catch(...) fallback alongside
  the std::exception catch. Both paths try-swallow the
  follow-up `send` to a dead transport.
* MCPServer::handleRequest — wrap the dispatch switch in
  try/catch; exceptions from handleInitialize /
  handleToolsList / handleToolsCall become JSON-RPC
  internalError responses with the caught message, not a
  thread termination.
* App::OnLaunched stdio branch — wrap MCPServerHost setup in
  try/catch + ExitProcess(2) so a constructor failure (audit
  logger folder create, settings parse) surfaces cleanly
  instead of aborting before Claude sees any output.
* Temporarily flip StdioTransport::kDebug to true so future
  stdio regressions leave a trail at
  %APPDATA%\Gridex\mcp-stdio-debug.log.

fix(mcp): warn before writing AppX/Debug path to Claude config

Root cause of 'abort() has been called' popup when Claude Desktop
connected to Gridex: the Install button stamped whatever exe
path the current process had into claude_desktop_config.json.
When the user was F5-ing an MSIX Debug AppX build from Visual
Studio, that path pointed at
 E:\dev\be\gridex\windows\x64\Debug\Gridex\AppX\Gridex.exe
which Claude cannot spawn as a plain child process — MSIX needs
package activation context, and without it the CRT aborts early
at load (before OnLaunched even runs, so our stdio hardening
couldn't catch it).

Guard in MCPPage::InstallClaude_Click now inspects
GetModuleFileNameW output and refuses to write the config if
the exe sits under an 'AppX' or 'Debug' folder; the status
label directs the user at the Release build (or the
build-unpackaged.ps1 self-contained output) which is what we
tested successfully via stdio pipe in this session.

fix(mcp): stop lying about prompts/resources capabilities — Claude CLI rejects

Claude CLI handshake flow:
  initialize -> server advertises capabilities
  tools/list -> ok
  prompts/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  resources/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  -> Claude CLI marks connection failed because the server
     advertised prompts + resources in its initialize response
     but then 404'd their list endpoints. It's a spec violation
     and the mac port inherited it because the Swift
     MCPServerInfo.gridex() stamped all four capability keys
     even though only tools was wired up.

Fix:
  * MCPServerInfo::mcpDefaultCapabilities — expose tools +
    logging only. Prompts / resources land when they actually
    have handlers.
  * MCPServer::handleRequest — handle prompts/list,
    resources/list, resources/templates/list by returning
    well-formed empty lists so clients that probe them anyway
    (Claude CLI does) see a healthy server instead of a
    methodNotFound disconnect trigger.
  * Also accept `notifications/initialized` (fully-qualified
    form Claude CLI uses) as a no-response notification.

Verified via smoke pipe: initialize -> 175 B (slimmer payload),
tools/list -> 1637 B (4 tools), prompts/list -> 49 B empty,
resources/list -> 51 B empty, EOF clean.

fix(mcp): use ConnectionConfig.password from ConnectionStore, not empty vault

fe_sendauth: no password supplied — PostgreSQL rejected tool-level
connects because MCPToolContext::getAdapter pulled the password
from CredentialManager (Windows Credential Vault), which Gridex
never writes to. Passwords actually live DPAPI-encrypted in the
SQLite `password_enc` column; ConnectionStore::Load decrypts them
into ConnectionConfig::password.

Read the password directly off the ConnectionConfig we already
loaded. Removed the stale CredentialManager include.

fix(import): drop follow-up ContentDialog + guard CheckBox reads post-dismiss

User reported crash after Import Selected — sidebar didn't
refresh, app terminated. Two interacting issues:

1. Snapshotting CheckBox.IsChecked() AFTER `co_await op` meant
   the controls were already mid-teardown when we read them.
   WinUI 3 can throw from the getter once the dialog starts
   animating out; the throw propagated unhandled from the
   fire_and_forget coroutine and killed the process.

2. Back-to-back ContentDialogs on the same XamlRoot (import
   dialog → "Import Complete" confirmation) are historically
   fragile in WinUI 3 — even when the first has resolved, the
   second ShowAsync can throw if teardown isn't fully done.

Fix:
* Wrap the whole ShowAsync + co_await in try/catch, drop out
  on any exception.
* Snapshot selected indices into a plain vector INSIDE a
  per-checkbox try/catch, then close the dialog scope before
  touching ConnectionStore.
* Every Save() call individually try/wrapped so one bad row
  can't abort the batch.
* Remove the follow-up ContentDialog entirely. User already
  sees the new rows appear in the sidebar (RefreshList now
  re-reads the store from the previous commit); a separate
  toast is redundant and was the crash trigger.

fix(import): buffer overflow in newConnectionId crashed import save

feat(clickhouse): add ClickHouse adapter via HTTP interface

Full PG-adapter parity for ClickHouse connections. Transport: HTTP
port 8123 using cpp-httplib (avoids clickhouse-cpp's abseil build

fix(clickhouse): winsock2 include order + drop SSLClient (httplib built w/o OpenSSL)

Three compile-breakers from the initial CH landing:

1. <windows.h> was included before <winsock2.h>, so the legacy
   winsock.h got dragged in first and clashed with winsock2 structs
   (sockaddr, fd_set, timeval…) — 100+ C2011 redefinition errors.
   Reordered: WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN + winsock2 + ws2tcpip first, then
   windows.h.

2. httplib::SSLClient is gated by CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT which
   the vendored build does not define. Dropped the TLS branch; plain
   httplib::Client only. Users needing TLS can front CH with
   nginx/Caddy and point us at the plaintext backend.

3. String-literal concat ('...' + '`' + db) — two pointers can't be
   added. Wrapped the first literal in std::string().

fix(clickhouse): currentSchema defaults to connected DB, drop built-in functions from sidebar

Two bugs were hiding user tables:

1. WorkspacePage default currentSchema_ = "public" (PG convention)
   had no ClickHouse branch, so listTables("public") / fetchRows
   kept looking for a non-existent public.<t>. Mirrored the MySQL
   branch — CH has no schemas, the database IS the schema.

2. listFunctions used origin='System' which returns ~1000 built-ins
   (BIT_AND, sumMap, …) and flooded the sidebar. Some sidebar paths
   even tried to open them as tables. Scoped to 'SQLUserDefined' so
   only user functions show, matching PG/MySQL behaviour.

and errored with 'Unknown table expression identifier' because
functions aren't tables.

Function clicks to ShowFunctionSource() which calls the adapter's
getFunctionSource() and drops the DDL into a fresh query tab.
Behaviour lines up with DataGrip/Navicat — user can tweak and

Also wired ClickHouseAdapter::getFunctionSource to read create_query
from system.functions (user-defined only; built-ins still return
empty and render as a stub comment).

fix(clickhouse): rewrite function source as CREATE OR REPLACE so Run is idempotent

CH's system.functions.create_query is the raw 'CREATE FUNCTION name
AS ...'. Clicking Run in the source-viewer tab hit FUNCTION_ALREADY_
EXISTS. CH 26 supports 'CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION', so swap the
prefix before handing the DDL to the UI. Run now re-creates the UDF
in place and doubles as a cheap edit flow.

Promote file-scope static helpers to public static members of
ERDiagramService so other services can reuse consistent D2 escaping,
temp-file, and d2.exe subprocess logic without copy-paste drift.

- SanitizeIdentifier / IsD2Reserved / QuoteIfReserved: D2 identifier
  rules extracted from GenerateD2Text internals.
- EscapeD2Label (new): wrap + escape a string for use as a D2 quoted
  label; handles embedded quotes, backslashes, newlines.
- TempPath: accepts an optional prefix param (default "er_" keeps
  existing behavior); counter upgraded to std::atomic<int> so distinct
  prefixes can share the filename namespace safely.
- RunD2: same signature, now a class method instead of file-scope.

Zero behavior change for existing callers — all internal call sites in
GenerateD2Text and Generate updated to use the new capitalized names.

* feat(windows): add row-relationship extension points to DataGridView + DatabaseAdapter

Opt-in extension points so downstream code (upcoming enterprise row
relationship graph feature) can hook into row right-click actions and
assemble safe SQL for the active engine without fork-patching OSS.

DataGridView
- New public callback OnViewRelationshipsRequested.

DatabaseAdapter
- New virtual quoteSqlLiteral and quoteSqlIdentifier, both with a
  default impl that throws. Non-SQL adapters (Mongo, Redis) inherit
  the throw so accidental calls fail loudly instead of silently
  producing wrong SQL.
- PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite / MSSQL override both, delegating to the
  existing utf8 quoteLiteral / quoteIdentifier helpers and converting
  the result back to wstring.

Zero behavior change for existing call paths — the new virtuals are
additive API, and the DataGridView item is hidden unless opted in.

* fix(mcp): HTTP transport + 6 correctness fixes + UI parity round 1

Review flagged P0 blocker: HttpOnly mode started a server with NO
listening transport ('TODO Phase 4d'), so GUI 'Start Server' set
running=true but no client could ever connect. Fixed by wiring
cpp-httplib on localhost:port. Plus 5 correctness fixes and 2
UI-parity additions matching screenshot_mac.

Correctness:
* HttpTransport via cpp-httplib (pimpl so OpenSSL/WinSock don't
  leak) — POST / and POST /mcp accept JSON-RPC, GET /health for
  ops. Binds 127.0.0.1 by default, 0.0.0.0 when
  AppSettings.mcpAllowRemoteHTTP set. Wired into MCPServer for
  HttpOnly mode.
* Fix UAF in MCPServerHost::instance() — return shared_ptr so
  callers can't dereference after a concurrent stop().
* Fix QueryTool forcing `LIMIT n` on MSSQL Server (invalid syntax).
  Only append LIMIT for Postgres/MySQL/SQLite.
* Fix MCPTool::extractConnectionId char-by-char widening that
  corrupted non-ASCII ids — proper MultiByteToWideChar.
* Fix MCPAuditEntry.inputHash non-deterministic (std::hash is
  randomized on MSVC). Switch to FNV-1a 64 for stable cross-run
  correlation.
* StdioTransport: switch from std::cin/std::cout to raw Win32
  HANDLE I/O (ReadFile/WriteFile on GetStdHandle). Gridex is GUI
  subsystem so C runtime stdio isn't auto-wired; inherited pipe
  handles ARE available via GetStdHandle though. Kept a kDebug
  flag mirroring events to %APPDATA%\Gridex\mcp-stdio-debug.log
  for bring-up.
* MCPServer has explicit out-of-line dtor so HttpTransport pimpl
  (std::unique_ptr<Impl>) doesn't trigger incomplete-type errors
  in MCPServer.cpp.

* fix(mcp): null-guard Pivot lazy-load so opening MCP Server doesn't crash

Pivot in WinUI 3 lazy-realizes PivotItem content — only the
selected tab's controls exist at page Loaded. The original
RefreshUI eagerly touched x:Name controls on all 5 tabs, so
navigating from HomePage to MCPPage crashed inside
consume_Microsoft_UI_Xaml_Controls_IPanel::Children() with
nullptr abi_type (observed: read access violation when calling
HttpToggle/QpmBox/etc that live in the Config tab).

Fix:
* Hook Pivot.SelectionChanged -> dispatches to the tab-specific
  Refresh* function when that tab first becomes active.
* Loaded only calls RefreshUI (overview-only path).
* RefreshUI now null-guards each tab's control group so it works
  regardless of which tabs are materialized.
* RefreshConnectionsTab / RefreshActivityTab early-return when
  their panels are nullptr.
* Entire Loaded handler wrapped in try/catch so a future refresh
  bug never prevents navigation.

* fix(mcp): harden stdio reader so Claude Desktop connect never aborts

Debug popup "abort() has been called" fired from the AppX Debug
build when Claude Desktop connected to Gridex --mcp-stdio. Root
cause: an uncaught exception on the reader thread escaped the
existing std::exception-only catch block; Debug CRT turned the
resulting std::terminate into abort() + popup.

Harden every cross-thread boundary so a single malformed
request or SEH escape can never crash the whole server:

* StdioTransport::readLoop — add catch(...) fallback alongside
  the std::exception catch. Both paths try-swallow the
  follow-up `send` to a dead transport.
* MCPServer::handleRequest — wrap the dispatch switch in
  try/catch; exceptions from handleInitialize /
  handleToolsList / handleToolsCall become JSON-RPC
  internalError responses with the caught message, not a
  thread termination.
* App::OnLaunched stdio branch — wrap MCPServerHost setup in
  try/catch + ExitProcess(2) so a constructor failure (audit
  logger folder create, settings parse) surfaces cleanly
  instead of aborting before Claude sees any output.
* Temporarily flip StdioTransport::kDebug to true so future
  stdio regressions leave a trail at
  %APPDATA%\Gridex\mcp-stdio-debug.log.

* fix(mcp): warn before writing AppX/Debug path to Claude config

Root cause of 'abort() has been called' popup when Claude Desktop
connected to Gridex: the Install button stamped whatever exe
path the current process had into claude_desktop_config.json.
When the user was F5-ing an MSIX Debug AppX build from Visual
Studio, that path pointed at
 E:\dev\be\gridex\windows\x64\Debug\Gridex\AppX\Gridex.exe
which Claude cannot spawn as a plain child process — MSIX needs
package activation context, and without it the CRT aborts early
at load (before OnLaunched even runs, so our stdio hardening
couldn't catch it).

Guard in MCPPage::InstallClaude_Click now inspects
GetModuleFileNameW output and refuses to write the config if
the exe sits under an 'AppX' or 'Debug' folder; the status
label directs the user at the Release build (or the
build-unpackaged.ps1 self-contained output) which is what we
tested successfully via stdio pipe in this session.

* fix(mcp): stop lying about prompts/resources capabilities — Claude CLI rejects

Claude CLI handshake flow:
  initialize -> server advertises capabilities
  tools/list -> ok
  prompts/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  resources/list -> we returned methodNotFound
  -> Claude CLI marks connection failed because the server
     advertised prompts + resources in its initialize response
     but then 404'd their list endpoints. It's a spec violation
     and the mac port inherited it because the Swift
     MCPServerInfo.gridex() stamped all four capability keys
     even though only tools was wired up.

Fix:
  * MCPServerInfo::mcpDefaultCapabilities — expose tools +
    logging only. Prompts / resources land when they actually
    have handlers.
  * MCPServer::handleRequest — handle prompts/list,
    resources/list, resources/templates/list by returning
    well-formed empty lists so clients that probe them anyway
    (Claude CLI does) see a healthy server instead of a
    methodNotFound disconnect trigger.
  * Also accept `notifications/initialized` (fully-qualified
    form Claude CLI uses) as a no-response notification.

Verified via smoke pipe: initialize -> 175 B (slimmer payload),
tools/list -> 1637 B (4 tools), prompts/list -> 49 B empty,
resources/list -> 51 B empty, EOF clean.

* fix(mcp): use ConnectionConfig.password from ConnectionStore, not empty vault

fe_sendauth: no password supplied — PostgreSQL rejected tool-level
connects because MCPToolContext::getAdapter pulled the password
from CredentialManager (Windows Credential Vault), which Gridex
never writes to. Passwords actually live DPAPI-encrypted in the
SQLite `password_enc` column; ConnectionStore::Load decrypts them
into ConnectionConfig::password.

Read the password directly off the ConnectionConfig we already
loaded. Removed the stale CredentialManager include.

* feat(mcp): Round 1B — 4 Tier-3 write tools with approval gate

All destructive MCP tools from mac now land on Windows. Each
goes through MCPApprovalGate (ContentDialog on MainWindow XamlRoot)

* fix(mcp): persist HTTP toggle + port on change, gate HTTP listen on flag

Two bugs rolled into one user report "bật lên mà không thấy nút
save bấm ra là mất":

1. HttpToggle_Toggled only flipped the port-row visibility and
   never wrote mcpHttpEnabled back to AppSettings. Every time the
   user left the page the state reverted to whatever was last
   saved. Now the handler auto-saves on change (Overview tab
   has no dedicated Save button for a single toggle).

2. MCPServer::start bound the HTTP listener unconditionally in
   HttpOnly mode — the mcpHttpEnabled flag was only used to pick
   the port value, so "HTTP off" still had a server listening on
   3333. Gate the entire bind block on settings_.mcpHttpEnabled
   instead. When the toggle is off we register tools + audit but
   don't open any socket; user can flip the toggle + restart to
   listen.

Also:
* HttpPortBox.ValueChanged auto-saves the port the same way.
* Hint in RunningSubtitle when the user toggles while a server
  is already running — HTTP listener doesn't hot-swap.
* HTTP handler mirrors the stdio dispatch for prompts/list,
  resources/list, resources/templates/list, notifications/
  initialized — same Claude-CLI handshake parity we already
  added for stdio.

fix(mcp): don't reply to JSON-RPC notifications; correct Linux client paths (#32)

Two Linux-specific MCP fixes that were blocking Claude Code integration.

1. JSON-RPC notifications received an unsolicited response.

   The transport handler was sending a response for every incoming request,
   including notifications like `initialized`. Claude Code validates each
   response with zod and rejects `id: null`, drops the stdio connection,
   and marks the server as failed right after `initialize` succeeds.

   Gate the send on `!req.id.is_null()` so notifications are silent per
   the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec. Verified end-to-end with `claude mcp list`
   and direct tool calls (list_connections, list_tables, query).

2. Setup tab listed clients with macOS/Windows paths.

   Claude Desktop is not available on Linux, and the Claude Code / Windsurf
   paths differed from the earlier entries. Replace the client list with
   Linux-correct paths:

     Claude Code  -> ~/.claude.json         (top-level mcpServers)
     Cursor       -> ~/.cursor/mcp.json
     Windsurf     -> ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json
     Gemini CLI   -> ~/.gemini/settings.json

   Claude Desktop is omitted (no Linux build).

fix(postgres): list all schemas via pg_namespace (#34)

Switch `listSchemas` from `information_schema.schemata` to `pg_namespace`.

The SQL-standard `information_schema.schemata` view filters its rows by
`pg_has_role(nspowner, 'USAGE') OR has_schema_privilege(nsp, 'USAGE, CREATE')`.
On Supabase the connecting `postgres` role is NOSUPERUSER, the internal
schemas (`auth`, `storage`, `realtime`, `extensions`, `graphql`) are owned
by `supabase_admin`, and no USAGE grant is issued — so every schema except
`public` silently vanishes from the sidebar.

`pg_namespace` is readable by any role and returns every physical schema,
matching the behaviour of pgAdmin / TablePlus / DBeaver. The same
system-schema exclusions are kept, plus a regex that drops transient
`pg_temp_*` / `pg_toast_temp_*` (which the old view was excluding for us).

If the current role can't USAGE a newly-visible schema, `listTables`
still returns empty rows silently (information_schema.tables also filters
by privilege), and attempting to read its data will throw a normal Postgres
permission error — the expected semantics; no new crash surface.

Verified with a local reproduction of Supabase's role layout
(`postgres` NOSUPERUSER, `supabase_admin` owning the internal schemas with
no USAGE grant): old query returned `public` only, new query returns all
six schemas, matching the user's report in #34.

fix(postgres): persist 5-state SSLMode and gate PostgresClient.run()

Two issues surfaced together while connecting HighGo Secure V4.5.7
(PostgreSQL fork) over PostgresNIO 1.32:

1. ConnectionPoolError race: querying immediately after spawning
   `Task { await client.run() }` could lease a connection before
   `run()` was scheduled, which PostgresNIO surfaces as a bare
   `_ConnectionPoolModule.ConnectionPoolError` and hides the real
   cause. Reproduces on slow handshakes (HighGo's login-audit NOTICE
   adds extra round-trips). Gate with `withCheckedContinuation` plus
   a trailing `Task.yield()` so `run()` reaches its first suspension
   point before the first lease.

2. SSLMode collapsed into a Bool (incident 6a4aad0 follow-up): the
   5-state UI picker (DISABLED / PREFERRED / REQUIRED / VERIFY_CA /
   VERIFY_IDENTITY) was persisted as `sslEnabled: Bool`, so REQUIRED
   and the two VERIFY_* modes silently degraded to `.prefer(tls)`.
   Add `sslMode: SSLMode?` to ConnectionConfig and SavedConnectionEntity
   (Optional for SwiftData lightweight migration / Codable back-compat),
   wire it through the form and repository, and centralize the legacy
   fallback in `ConnectionConfig.effectiveSSLMode`. The PostgreSQL
   adapter now honors all five modes via a private `makeTLSConfig`
   helper following libpq semantics — REQUIRED/VERIFY_* now actually
   require a TLS handshake instead of silently allowing plaintext.

Other adapters (MySQL/Mongo/Redis/MSSQL/ClickHouse) still consume the
legacy `sslEnabled` Bool; extending them to honor sslMode is left as
a follow-up.

fix(postgres): persist SSL certificate paths

Saved PostgreSQL connections could retain strict SSL modes without retaining the certificate paths that made those modes usable. After reload, VERIFY_CA, VERIFY_IDENTITY, or mTLS connections could lose their CA/client certificate configuration.

- Add optional SSL key, cert, and CA path fields to the SwiftData entity for lightweight migration compatibility

- Round-trip the paths through save, update, and toConfig so persisted connections keep the same TLS inputs

test(postgres): XCTest suite for SSLMode + race fix (PR #43 verification)

Adds the project's first XCTest target. 21 tests across 3 suites
verifying every claim in PR #43 (incident 6a4aad0 follow-up + the
HighGo handshake race).

Suites:

- SSLModeFallbackTests (5 pure-logic tests, no infra needed)
  • effectiveSSLMode prefers explicit SSLMode over legacy sslEnabled
  • legacy sslEnabled=true → .preferred (no silent upgrade)
  • legacy sslEnabled=false → .disabled
  • Codable decodes a pre-PR JSON payload (no sslMode field) cleanly
  • Codable round-trips an explicit mode + cert paths

- ConnectionRepositoryTests (4 SwiftData round-trip tests, in-memory)
  • save() then fetch preserves all three cert paths
  • update() preserves all three cert paths
  • Each of 5 SSLMode values round-trips through SwiftData
  • Legacy row (sslMode=nil) reads back as effectiveSSLMode=.preferred

- PostgreSQLAdapterIntegrationTests (12 tests against real PG)
  Skipped automatically when PG isn't reachable on 127.0.0.1:55434
  / :55435. Setup is a no-SSL PG plus an ssl=on PG with a self-signed
  cert (CN=localhost) under /tmp/gridex-pg-certs/.

  vs no-SSL server:
    disabled                                → succeeds
    preferred                               → succeeds (plaintext fallback)
    required          (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS  ← bug #2 receipt
    verifyCA          (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS
    verifyIdentity    (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS

  vs SSL server:
    disabled                                → succeeds
    required                                → succeeds
    verifyCA + correct CA (host=127.0.0.1)  → succeeds (chain only)
    verifyCA + wrong CA                     → FAILS
    verifyIdentity (host=127.0.0.1, CN=localhost) → FAILS  (matches psql)
    verifyIdentity (host=localhost, CN=localhost) → succeeds

  Race fix: 20 rapid connect→SELECT 1→disconnect cycles, no
  ConnectionPoolError surfaces.

All 21 tests pass on the PR #43 head. Pre-PR they would fail in the
predictable spots (the four "must FAIL" SSL tests would all silently
succeed because .prefer(tls) was used; cert path tests would lose
the paths on round-trip).

Caveats:

- This branch is stacked on PR #43; a clean PR (base=main) will
  open after #43 merges. Pushed here so reviewers can run the suite
  against #43 immediately.
- Suite runtime ~340s, dominated by 5 fail-expected tests that wait
  PostgresNIO's full retry cycle (~68s each). A connectionTimeout on
  ConnectionConfig would cut this; out of scope for this commit.
- Test target compiles against the executable target via @testable;
  that works on Swift 5.10+. The executable's Info.plist linker flag
  doesn't propagate to the test bundle.

fix(postgres): exclude partition children from listTables

Follow-up to the listTables migration in this PR.

`relkind IN ('r', 'p')` returns ordinary tables (`r`) and partitioned-table
parents (`p`), but partition CHILDREN are also `r` rows — the parent already
represents their data, so leaking them would surface every partition as a
sibling table in the sidebar and double-count rows.

The original `information_schema.tables WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE'`
query returned only parents; switching to pg_class without filtering
introduces a regression for any user with declarative partitioning
(common on PG 11+ for time-series, multi-tenant, analytics workloads).

Add `AND NOT c.relispartition` to restore the original semantics.
`relispartition` exists since PG 10 (when declarative partitioning shipped),
so no version concern.

Verified locally: pre-fix returned 4 rows (parent + 1 child + 2 plain) for
a fixture with one partitioned table; post-fix returns 3 rows (parent +
2 plain) matching the pre-PR information_schema behavior.

Also adds `test_listTables_excludesPartitionChildren_onVanillaPG` to the
existing integration suite — runs against the local PG :55434 instance,
creates a fixture with a partitioned-table parent and one child, asserts
the parent is visible but the child is not. Test verifies both directions:
removing the fix makes the assertion fail (confirmed by stash + re-run).

Drops the per-method `Logger`/`import Logging` added alongside the
information_schema → pg_class shift: only `listTables` was instrumented
while the other ten metadata methods in this file are not, and `Logging`
isn't declared in Package.swift (resolves transitively through PostgresNIO
which is brittle to future bumps). Either log everywhere consistently in
a follow-up, or not here.

fix(query): per-engine EXPLAIN syntax, fixes #49

The query editor's `Explain` button always sent
`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN <sql>` — that's SQLite-specific. Postgres rejects it
with `syntax error at or near "QUERY"` (SQLSTATE 42601, position 9), and
the same shape breaks MySQL / SQL Server / ClickHouse.

The MCP `explain_query` tool already had a per-engine `switch` (PG uses
`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE false, COSTS true, FORMAT TEXT)`, MSSQL uses
`SET SHOWPLAN_TEXT ON; …; SET SHOWPLAN_TEXT OFF`, etc.), but the editor
button bypassed it — duplicate logic that drifted into a hardcoded
SQLite-only path.

- New extension `DatabaseType.explainSQL(for:)` centralises the per-engine
  syntax. Returns nil for Mongo / Redis (no SQL EXPLAIN concept) so
  callers can show a clean message instead of forwarding garbage to the
  server.
- `QueryEditorView.explainQuery()` now goes through the helper; on nil
  the editor surfaces "EXPLAIN is not supported for <engine> connections."
  inline.
- `ExplainQueryTool` (MCP) drops its own switch and reuses the helper —
  one source of truth.

Tests
- `DatabaseTypeExplainTests` — 10 pure-logic cases pinning the SQL shape
  per engine, the nil contract for Mongo / Redis, blank-input handling,
  and an exhaustiveness loop over `DatabaseType.allCases`. Locks the
  receipt for #49 explicitly: PG output must NEVER contain "QUERY PLAN".
- `PostgreSQLAdapterIntegrationTests` — adds
  `test_explainSQL_postgresShape_runsWithoutSyntaxError` against local
  PG :55434 to confirm the produced SQL actually parses and returns a
  plan.

11 new tests, all pass.

fix(postgres): exclude partition children from listTables

Follow-up to the listTables migration in this PR.

`relkind IN ('r', 'p')` returns ordinary tables (`r`) and partitioned-table
parents (`p`), but partition CHILDREN are also `r` rows — the parent already
represents their data, so leaking them would surface every partition as a
sibling table in the sidebar and double-count rows.

The original `information_schema.tables WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE'`
query returned only parents; switching to pg_class without filtering
introduces a regression for any user with declarative partitioning
(common on PG 11+ for time-series, multi-tenant, analytics workloads).

Add `AND NOT c.relispartition` to restore the original semantics.
`relispartition` exists since PG 10 (when declarative partitioning shipped),
so no version concern.

Verified locally: pre-fix returned 4 rows (parent + 1 child + 2 plain) for
a fixture with one partitioned table; post-fix returns 3 rows (parent +
2 plain) matching the pre-PR information_schema behavior.

Also adds `test_listTables_excludesPartitionChildren_onVanillaPG` to the
existing integration suite — runs against the local PG :55434 instance,
creates a fixture with a partitioned-table parent and one child, asserts
the parent is visible but the child is not. Test verifies both directions:
removing the fix makes the assertion fail (confirmed by stash + re-run).

Drops the per-method `Logger`/`import Logging` added alongside the
information_schema → pg_class shift: only `listTables` was instrumented
while the other ten metadata methods in this file are not, and `Logging`
isn't declared in Package.swift (resolves transitively through PostgresNIO
which is brittle to future bumps). Either log everywhere consistently in
a follow-up, or not here.

fix(postgres): persist 5-state SSLMode and gate PostgresClient.run()

Two issues surfaced together while connecting HighGo Secure V4.5.7
(PostgreSQL fork) over PostgresNIO 1.32:

1. ConnectionPoolError race: querying immediately after spawning
   `Task { await client.run() }` could lease a connection before
   `run()` was scheduled, which PostgresNIO surfaces as a bare
   `_ConnectionPoolModule.ConnectionPoolError` and hides the real
   cause. Reproduces on slow handshakes (HighGo's login-audit NOTICE
   adds extra round-trips). Gate with `withCheckedContinuation` plus
   a trailing `Task.yield()` so `run()` reaches its first suspension
   point before the first lease.

2. SSLMode collapsed into a Bool (incident 6a4aad0 follow-up): the
   5-state UI picker (DISABLED / PREFERRED / REQUIRED / VERIFY_CA /
   VERIFY_IDENTITY) was persisted as `sslEnabled: Bool`, so REQUIRED
   and the two VERIFY_* modes silently degraded to `.prefer(tls)`.
   Add `sslMode: SSLMode?` to ConnectionConfig and SavedConnectionEntity
   (Optional for SwiftData lightweight migration / Codable back-compat),
   wire it through the form and repository, and centralize the legacy
   fallback in `ConnectionConfig.effectiveSSLMode`. The PostgreSQL
   adapter now honors all five modes via a private `makeTLSConfig`
   helper following libpq semantics — REQUIRED/VERIFY_* now actually
   require a TLS handshake instead of silently allowing plaintext.

Other adapters (MySQL/Mongo/Redis/MSSQL/ClickHouse) still consume the
legacy `sslEnabled` Bool; extending them to honor sslMode is left as
a follow-up.

fix(postgres): persist SSL certificate paths

Saved PostgreSQL connections could retain strict SSL modes without retaining the certificate paths that made those modes usable. After reload, VERIFY_CA, VERIFY_IDENTITY, or mTLS connections could lose their CA/client certificate configuration.

- Add optional SSL key, cert, and CA path fields to the SwiftData entity for lightweight migration compatibility

- Round-trip the paths through save, update, and toConfig so persisted connections keep the same TLS inputs

test(postgres): XCTest suite for SSLMode + race fix (PR #43 verification)

Adds the project's first XCTest target. 21 tests across 3 suites
verifying every claim in PR #43 (incident 6a4aad0 follow-up + the
HighGo handshake race).

Suites:

- SSLModeFallbackTests (5 pure-logic tests, no infra needed)
  • effectiveSSLMode prefers explicit SSLMode over legacy sslEnabled
  • legacy sslEnabled=true → .preferred (no silent upgrade)
  • legacy sslEnabled=false → .disabled
  • Codable decodes a pre-PR JSON payload (no sslMode field) cleanly
  • Codable round-trips an explicit mode + cert paths

- ConnectionRepositoryTests (4 SwiftData round-trip tests, in-memory)
  • save() then fetch preserves all three cert paths
  • update() preserves all three cert paths
  • Each of 5 SSLMode values round-trips through SwiftData
  • Legacy row (sslMode=nil) reads back as effectiveSSLMode=.preferred

- PostgreSQLAdapterIntegrationTests (12 tests against real PG)
  Skipped automatically when PG isn't reachable on 127.0.0.1:55434
  / :55435. Setup is a no-SSL PG plus an ssl=on PG with a self-signed
  cert (CN=localhost) under /tmp/gridex-pg-certs/.

  vs no-SSL server:
    disabled                                → succeeds
    preferred                               → succeeds (plaintext fallback)
    required          (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS  ← bug #2 receipt
    verifyCA          (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS
    verifyIdentity    (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS

  vs SSL server:
    disabled                                → succeeds
    required                                → succeeds
    verifyCA + correct CA (host=127.0.0.1)  → succeeds (chain only)
    verifyCA + wrong CA                     → FAILS
    verifyIdentity (host=127.0.0.1, CN=localhost) → FAILS  (matches psql)
    verifyIdentity (host=localhost, CN=localhost) → succeeds

  Race fix: 20 rapid connect→SELECT 1→disconnect cycles, no
  ConnectionPoolError surfaces.

All 21 tests pass on the PR #43 head. Pre-PR they would fail in the
predictable spots (the four "must FAIL" SSL tests would all silently
succeed because .prefer(tls) was used; cert path tests would lose
the paths on round-trip).

Caveats:

- This branch is stacked on PR #43; a clean PR (base=main) will
  open after #43 merges. Pushed here so reviewers can run the suite
  against #43 immediately.
- Suite runtime ~340s, dominated by 5 fail-expected tests that wait
  PostgresNIO's full retry cycle (~68s each). A connectionTimeout on
  ConnectionConfig would cut this; out of scope for this commit.
- Test target compiles against the executable target via @testable;
  that works on Swift 5.10+. The executable's Info.plist linker flag
  doesn't propagate to the test bundle.

fix(postgres): exclude partition children from listTables

Follow-up to the listTables migration in this PR.

`relkind IN ('r', 'p')` returns ordinary tables (`r`) and partitioned-table
parents (`p`), but partition CHILDREN are also `r` rows — the parent already
represents their data, so leaking them would surface every partition as a
sibling table in the sidebar and double-count rows.

The original `information_schema.tables WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE'`
query returned only parents; switching to pg_class without filtering
introduces a regression for any user with declarative partitioning
(common on PG 11+ for time-series, multi-tenant, analytics workloads).

Add `AND NOT c.relispartition` to restore the original semantics.
`relispartition` exists since PG 10 (when declarative partitioning shipped),
so no version concern.

Verified locally: pre-fix returned 4 rows (parent + 1 child + 2 plain) for
a fixture with one partitioned table; post-fix returns 3 rows (parent +
2 plain) matching the pre-PR information_schema behavior.

Also adds `test_listTables_excludesPartitionChildren_onVanillaPG` to the
existing integration suite — runs against the local PG :55434 instance,
creates a fixture with a partitioned-table parent and one child, asserts
the parent is visible but the child is not. Test verifies both directions:
removing the fix makes the assertion fail (confirmed by stash + re-run).

Drops the per-method `Logger`/`import Logging` added alongside the
information_schema → pg_class shift: only `listTables` was instrumented
while the other ten metadata methods in this file are not, and `Logging`
isn't declared in Package.swift (resolves transitively through PostgresNIO
which is brittle to future bumps). Either log everywhere consistently in
a follow-up, or not here.

feat(linux): ClickHouse adapter via HTTP interface (#59)

Sixth database adapter, mirroring the macOS / Windows ports. Speaks the
ClickHouse HTTP API (port 8123 plain / 8443 TLS) using Qt Network with a
blocking event loop, matching the synchronous shape of IDatabaseAdapter.

Backend (Data/Adapters/ClickHouse/ClickhouseAdapter.{h,cpp}):
* JSONCompact for SELECT/EXPLAIN/SHOW/DESCRIBE/WITH; plain statements
  otherwise. Type unwrap covers Nullable(T), Array, Map, Tuple, JSON,
  UInt*, Int*, Float*, Decimal, UUID, Date*, String, Bool, FixedString,
  Enum*, with safe fallback to JSON or string.
* USE statement intercept — CH HTTP is stateless, so the adapter
  transparently updates the in-memory default database for follow-up
  queries.
* DML: INSERT VALUES, ALTER TABLE … UPDATE/DELETE for MergeTree-family
  engines. ensureMutable() pre-checks system.tables.engine and surfaces
  a clear error for Log/View/Dictionary engines that can't mutate.
* Schema introspection from system.databases / system.tables /
  system.columns / system.data_skipping_indices. Caches server version
  on connect so the is_in_primary_key flag (CH 21.3+) is used when
  available with a graceful fallback for older versions.
* listSchemas() returns [currentDatabase()] so the workspace sidebar
  renders the active DB as the schema node (mirrors MySQL's behaviour
  for flat databases).
* Transactions are no-ops (CH has no traditional ACID transactions).

Wiring:
* DatabaseType::ClickHouse and SQLDialect::ClickHouse with
  defaultPort=8123 (8443 when sslEnabled). Backtick-quoted identifiers.
* AdapterFactory routes to the new adapter.
* nlohmann/json FetchContent moves to the top-level CMakeLists so both
  Data and Services can link nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json without
  worrying about add_subdirectory ordering.
* Qt6::Network linked into gridex-data for the HTTP transport.

ClickHouse appears in the type combo automatically with the generic
host/port/user/pass/db layout.

* Connect with default:test123 to localhost:8123, database `demo`.
* Sidebar lists `demo` schema with `events` (5 rows) and `users` (3 rows).
* SELECT JOIN across both tables returns expected rows with mixed types
  (LowCardinality, Nullable, Decimal, DateTime, Date, Bool, Uint*).
* ALTER TABLE … UPDATE/DELETE on MergeTree succeeds; the same on a Log

feat(linux): Sign in with ChatGPT (OAuth + provider client) (#60)

Ports the macOS / Windows ChatGPT OAuth flow so the Linux build can
authenticate against an OpenAI subscription via the public Codex CLI
client_id rather than requiring a paid platform API key. Mirrors the
macOS file layout one-to-one.

OAuth core (Services/AI/Auth/):
* ChatGPTOAuthConstants.h — issuer, client_id, scopes, ports, timeouts.
* PKCE.{h,cpp} — RFC 7636 verifier/challenge/state + base64url helpers
  on top of QRandomGenerator + QCryptographicHash.
* JwtDecoder.{h,cpp} — payload decode for `exp` / `email` /
  `chatgpt_account_id` / `chatgpt_plan_type` (no signature verification —
  issuer is reached over TLS).
* OAuthLoopbackServer.{h,cpp} — single-shot QTcpServer bound to
  127.0.0.1:1455-1458 (ephemeral fallback), parses the GET callback,
  serves a Catppuccin-styled "you can close this tab" page, calls back
  with code+state. Times out after 180 s.
* ChatGPTOAuthService.{h,cpp} — orchestrates signIn / refresh / signOut /
  status. Persists the token bundle via SecretStore (libsecret). Auto-
  refresh request and refresh-token-rejected handling (wipes bundle on
  refresh_token_expired/reused/invalidated). Browser is opened via
  xdg-open through QProcess so the service library does not pull in
  Qt6::Gui.

LLM provider (Services/AI/Providers/ChatGPTProvider.{h,cpp}):
* Synchronous ILLMService using QEventLoop'd Qt Network calls — matches
  the existing AnthropicProvider pattern.
* In-process token refresh: load bundle from libsecret → if access_token
  is within kRefreshSkewSeconds of `exp`, POST /oauth/token with
  refresh_token blocking → persist rotated bundle → use new access_token.
* sendMessage() → POST chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses with the
  Codex-CLI wire format (instructions = system prompt; input = typed
  message items with input_text / output_text content parts;
  stream:true, store:false). Walks the SSE byte stream and accumulates
  `response.output_text.delta` payloads into a single string.
* availableModels() → GET /models?client_version=1.0.0 with the bearer
  + ChatGPT-Account-ID headers; filters to supported_in_api &&
  visibility==list to drop hidden / deprecated entries.
* 401/403 wipes the bundle and surfaces AuthenticationError so the UI
  prompts re-sign-in.

Storage (Data/Keychain/SecretStore.h):
* Adds save/load/delete helpers under the "ai.chatgpt.tokens.<key>"
  namespace, mirroring the existing API-key + DB-password conventions.

Models (Core/Models/AI/ChatGPTTokenBundle.h):
* Plain struct with toJson/fromJson — single source of truth for the
  serialized bundle layout (access/refresh/id token + decoded claims +
  obtainedAt epoch).

* AIServiceFactory routes "ChatGPT" to ChatGPTProvider.
* CMake adds the new sources to gridex-services.

fix(grid): re-introspect schema on Cmd+R and sidebar double-click (#63)

Cmd+R was calling `loadPage()` which re-fetched rows but never updated
`viewModel.columns`. When the table schema had changed externally
(e.g. someone ran ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN), the grid would render new
row data against the stale column list, shifting values into the wrong
columns or producing trailing NULLs.

Single-clicking an already-open table in the sidebar also did nothing —
`AppState.openTable` short-circuited to focus the existing tab without
any reload signal — so users had no visible way to refresh.

The view model already exposed `reloadAfterStructureChange()`, which
invalidates the static `metadataCache[cacheKey]` and runs a full
`load()` (rows + columns + PK + FK + enum metadata). Wire that into:

* DataGridView — Cmd+R handler and the discard-pending-changes path
  both call `reloadAfterStructureChange()` instead of `loadPage()`.
* SidebarView — added an `.onTapGesture(count: 2)` on table/view rows
  that focuses the tab and posts `.reloadData`. Single-click semantics
  are unchanged.

Workaround prior to this fix was to disconnect and reconnect the whole
connection.

fix(postgres): persist 5-state SSLMode and gate PostgresClient.run()

Two issues surfaced together while connecting HighGo Secure V4.5.7
(PostgreSQL fork) over PostgresNIO 1.32:

1. ConnectionPoolError race: querying immediately after spawning
   `Task { await client.run() }` could lease a connection before
   `run()` was scheduled, which PostgresNIO surfaces as a bare
   `_ConnectionPoolModule.ConnectionPoolError` and hides the real
   cause. Reproduces on slow handshakes (HighGo's login-audit NOTICE
   adds extra round-trips). Gate with `withCheckedContinuation` plus
   a trailing `Task.yield()` so `run()` reaches its first suspension
   point before the first lease.

2. SSLMode collapsed into a Bool (incident 6a4aad0 follow-up): the
   5-state UI picker (DISABLED / PREFERRED / REQUIRED / VERIFY_CA /
   VERIFY_IDENTITY) was persisted as `sslEnabled: Bool`, so REQUIRED
   and the two VERIFY_* modes silently degraded to `.prefer(tls)`.
   Add `sslMode: SSLMode?` to ConnectionConfig and SavedConnectionEntity
   (Optional for SwiftData lightweight migration / Codable back-compat),
   wire it through the form and repository, and centralize the legacy
   fallback in `ConnectionConfig.effectiveSSLMode`. The PostgreSQL
   adapter now honors all five modes via a private `makeTLSConfig`
   helper following libpq semantics — REQUIRED/VERIFY_* now actually
   require a TLS handshake instead of silently allowing plaintext.

Other adapters (MySQL/Mongo/Redis/MSSQL/ClickHouse) still consume the
legacy `sslEnabled` Bool; extending them to honor sslMode is left as
a follow-up.

fix(postgres): persist SSL certificate paths

Saved PostgreSQL connections could retain strict SSL modes without retaining the certificate paths that made those modes usable. After reload, VERIFY_CA, VERIFY_IDENTITY, or mTLS connections could lose their CA/client certificate configuration.

- Add optional SSL key, cert, and CA path fields to the SwiftData entity for lightweight migration compatibility

- Round-trip the paths through save, update, and toConfig so persisted connections keep the same TLS inputs

test(postgres): XCTest suite for SSLMode + race fix (PR #43 verification)

Adds the project's first XCTest target. 21 tests across 3 suites
verifying every claim in PR #43 (incident 6a4aad0 follow-up + the
HighGo handshake race).

Suites:

- SSLModeFallbackTests (5 pure-logic tests, no infra needed)
  • effectiveSSLMode prefers explicit SSLMode over legacy sslEnabled
  • legacy sslEnabled=true → .preferred (no silent upgrade)
  • legacy sslEnabled=false → .disabled
  • Codable decodes a pre-PR JSON payload (no sslMode field) cleanly
  • Codable round-trips an explicit mode + cert paths

- ConnectionRepositoryTests (4 SwiftData round-trip tests, in-memory)
  • save() then fetch preserves all three cert paths
  • update() preserves all three cert paths
  • Each of 5 SSLMode values round-trips through SwiftData
  • Legacy row (sslMode=nil) reads back as effectiveSSLMode=.preferred

- PostgreSQLAdapterIntegrationTests (12 tests against real PG)
  Skipped automatically when PG isn't reachable on 127.0.0.1:55434
  / :55435. Setup is a no-SSL PG plus an ssl=on PG with a self-signed
  cert (CN=localhost) under /tmp/gridex-pg-certs/.

  vs no-SSL server:
    disabled                                → succeeds
    preferred                               → succeeds (plaintext fallback)
    required          (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS  ← bug #2 receipt
    verifyCA          (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS
    verifyIdentity    (must enforce TLS)    → FAILS

  vs SSL server:
    disabled                                → succeeds
    required                                → succeeds
    verifyCA + correct CA (host=127.0.0.1)  → succeeds (chain only)
    verifyCA + wrong CA                     → FAILS
    verifyIdentity (host=127.0.0.1, CN=localhost) → FAILS  (matches psql)
    verifyIdentity (host=localhost, CN=localhost) → succeeds

  Race fix: 20 rapid connect→SELECT 1→disconnect cycles, no
  ConnectionPoolError surfaces.

All 21 tests pass on the PR #43 head. Pre-PR they would fail in the
predictable spots (the four "must FAIL" SSL tests would all silently
succeed because .prefer(tls) was used; cert path tests would lose
the paths on round-trip).

Caveats:

- This branch is stacked on PR #43; a clean PR (base=main) will
  open after #43 merges. Pushed here so reviewers can run the suite
  against #43 immediately.
- Suite runtime ~340s, dominated by 5 fail-expected tests that wait
  PostgresNIO's full retry cycle (~68s each). A connectionTimeout on
  ConnectionConfig would cut this; out of scope for this commit.
- Test target compiles against the executable target via @testable;
  that works on Swift 5.10+. The executable's Info.plist linker flag
  doesn't propagate to the test bundle.

fix(postgres): exclude partition children from listTables

Follow-up to the listTables migration in this PR.

`relkind IN ('r', 'p')` returns ordinary tables (`r`) and partitioned-table
parents (`p`), but partition CHILDREN are also `r` rows — the parent already
represents their data, so leaking them would surface every partition as a
sibling table in the sidebar and double-count rows.

The original `information_schema.tables WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE'`
query returned only parents; switching to pg_class without filtering
introduces a regression for any user with declarative partitioning
(common on PG 11+ for time-series, multi-tenant, analytics workloads).

Add `AND NOT c.relispartition` to restore the original semantics.
`relispartition` exists since PG 10 (when declarative partitioning shipped),
so no version concern.

Verified locally: pre-fix returned 4 rows (parent + 1 child + 2 plain) for
a fixture with one partitioned table; post-fix returns 3 rows (parent +
2 plain) matching the pre-PR information_schema behavior.

Also adds `test_listTables_excludesPartitionChildren_onVanillaPG` to the
existing integration suite — runs against the local PG :55434 instance,
creates a fixture with a partitioned-table parent and one child, asserts
the parent is visible but the child is not. Test verifies both directions:
removing the fix makes the assertion fail (confirmed by stash + re-run).

Drops the per-method `Logger`/`import Logging` added alongside the
information_schema → pg_class shift: only `listTables` was instrumented
while the other ten metadata methods in this file are not, and `Logging`
isn't declared in Package.swift (resolves transitively through PostgresNIO
which is brittle to future bumps). Either log everywhere consistently in
a follow-up, or not here.
