feat(query): rich EXPLAIN output panel — Text / JSON / Tree views

Replaces the raw-text dump after Explain with a 3-mode browser:

- **Text** — server output verbatim, monospace, optional word wrap
- **JSON** — JSONSerialization-prettified + lightweight syntax highlight
            (keys blue, strings red-ish, numbers green-ish, true/false
             /null purple, punctuation grey)
- **Tree** — recursive DisclosureGroup walk of the JSON plan, one
            collapsible node per `Plan` object with cost/rows/width
            summary line and the remaining primitive keys browsable
            as flat key/value rows underneath

Auto-picks Tree for `FORMAT JSON` output, Text otherwise. The Tree
segment hides itself for non-JSON output so the picker doesn't show a
non-functional option.

Toolbar in the panel: view-mode picker + Word Wrap toggle + Copy.

What this is NOT (intentionally — these belong in the Enterprise
Edition's `EEExplainVisualizerView`):
  - timing heatmap
  - planner-vs-actual misestimate detection (Rows X arrows)
  - slow-node / missing-index recommendations
  - Analysis-tab summary cards / Statistics tab

The OSS surface stops at "browse the plan as a tree without making any
decisions for the user".

Implementation
- `ExplainOutputView` — SwiftUI host with state for view mode + wrap.
  Hands off to one of three sub-views based on the picker.
- `ExplainJSONPrettyPrinter` — wraps JSONSerialization with
  `.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys, .withoutEscapingSlashes`. Returns nil
  on invalid input; caller falls back to raw.
- `ExplainJSONHighlightedText` — lexer-only syntax highlight (no
  parser). Tokenises strings / numbers / keywords / punctuation /
  whitespace and emits coloured `Text` segments. Treats a `"..."`
  followed by `:` as a key, otherwise as a string literal.
- `ExplainPlanReader` — parses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)` shape into a
  flat array of `ExplainPlanNode` (nodeType + summary string +
  attributes + children). Excludes Plan / Plans / Node Type / cost
  keys from the attribute list to avoid duplicate noise. CFBoolean
  type check distinguishes JSONSerialization's NSNumber-wrapped bools
  from numbers (a plain `as? Bool` would mis-classify 0/1).
- `ExplainPlanNodeRow` — DisclosureGroup per node. Read-only; click
  expands/collapses, no other interaction.
- `QueryEditorView` — new state `explainOutput: String?` +
  `explainOutputFormat: ExplainOptions.Format`. Set on Explain success,
  cleared on every Run, swaps in ExplainOutputView ahead of the data
  grid in the results pane render order.

Tests (11 new pure-logic)
- pretty-print: minified → reformatted, invalid → nil, sorted-keys
  stable across input order
- plan reader: single-node + nested (3-level) walks, sorted attribute
  list, cost/Plans keys excluded from attributes, real-ish PG 16
  ANALYZE+JSON output parses correctly, CFBoolean check surfaces
  booleans as "true"/"false" instead of "0"/"1"
- error paths: non-JSON, JSON-without-Plan-key, empty string

* feat(ai): port 'OpenAI (Sign in)' OAuth provider from mac PR #53

Adds ChatGPT subscription provider via the Codex CLI's public OAuth
client. Settings → Provider → 'OpenAI (Sign in)' opens the system
browser, runs the PKCE flow against auth.openai.com, captures the
redirect on a loopback HTTP listener, exchanges the code for tokens,
and stores them in a DPAPI-encrypted file under %APPDATA%\Gridex.
Subsequent chat calls use the bearer token against
chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses with SSE streaming.

Files added:
- Models/ChatGPTTokenBundle.h            token struct + JSON helpers
- Services/ChatGPTOAuth/PKCE.{h,cpp}     verifier/challenge via BCryptGenRandom + EVP_sha256 (base64url)
- Services/ChatGPTOAuth/JwtDecoder.{h,cpp}   base64url-decode payload, parse JSON, extract email + chatgpt_account_id + exp
- Services/ChatGPTOAuth/ChatGPTOAuthConstants.h  client_id, scopes, port 1455, refresh skew
- Services/ChatGPTOAuth/ChatGPTOAuthService.{h,cpp}  singleton: SignIn (browser + httplib::Server callback), refresh coalesced via mutex+shared_future, BearerToken/AccountId/CurrentEmail accessors

AiService:
- AiProvider::ChatGPT enum case (index 5)
- CallChatGPT — WinHTTP POST /backend-api/codex/responses, parses SSE
  delta events into accumulated text. 401/403 wipes tokens.
- FetchModels ChatGPT case — WinHTTP GET /backend-api/codex/models
  ?client_version=1.0.0 with Bearer + ChatGPT-Account-ID. Filters to
  models marked supported_in_api=true and visibility=list.

SettingsPage:
- New 'OpenAI (Sign in)' ComboBoxItem.
- ApiKeyPanel hides for ChatGPT; SignInPanel (status + Sign in/out)
  takes its place. OllamaEndpointPanel hides unless provider=Ollama.
- Sign-in success auto-clears Model dropdown and fetches the live
  list off /backend-api/codex/models so the previous provider's
  model name doesn't leak into the new session.

Why WinHTTP for ChatGPT only:
- Vcpkg cpp-httplib 0.40.0 + OpenSSL 3.x DLL has an ABI / threading
  mismatch — httplib::SSLClient destructor calls SSL_shutdown with
  a corrupted handle (s = 0x2) on the worker thread, fast-failing
  the process.
- Other providers (Anthropic / OpenAI / Ollama / Gemini / OpenRouter)
  still use httplib::Client because httplib auto-creates an
  SSLClient internally for https URLs and that path doesn't crash
  in practice for those hosts. Could migrate them later if needed.

- Single token file under %APPDATA%\Gridex\chatgpt-tokens.bin
  (no per-provider UUID — Windows settings model is single-active).
- Loopback listener uses cpp-httplib::Server in plain HTTP mode

- redirect_uri uses 'localhost' (not '127.0.0.1') because the
  registered Codex CLI client_id only accepts the literal hostname.

feat(linux): ClickHouse adapter via HTTP interface (#59)

Sixth database adapter, mirroring the macOS / Windows ports. Speaks the
ClickHouse HTTP API (port 8123 plain / 8443 TLS) using Qt Network with a
blocking event loop, matching the synchronous shape of IDatabaseAdapter.

Backend (Data/Adapters/ClickHouse/ClickhouseAdapter.{h,cpp}):
* JSONCompact for SELECT/EXPLAIN/SHOW/DESCRIBE/WITH; plain statements
  otherwise. Type unwrap covers Nullable(T), Array, Map, Tuple, JSON,
  UInt*, Int*, Float*, Decimal, UUID, Date*, String, Bool, FixedString,
  Enum*, with safe fallback to JSON or string.
* USE statement intercept — CH HTTP is stateless, so the adapter
  transparently updates the in-memory default database for follow-up
  queries.
* DML: INSERT VALUES, ALTER TABLE … UPDATE/DELETE for MergeTree-family
  engines. ensureMutable() pre-checks system.tables.engine and surfaces
  a clear error for Log/View/Dictionary engines that can't mutate.
* Schema introspection from system.databases / system.tables /
  system.columns / system.data_skipping_indices. Caches server version
  on connect so the is_in_primary_key flag (CH 21.3+) is used when
  available with a graceful fallback for older versions.
* listSchemas() returns [currentDatabase()] so the workspace sidebar
  renders the active DB as the schema node (mirrors MySQL's behaviour
  for flat databases).
* Transactions are no-ops (CH has no traditional ACID transactions).

Wiring:
* DatabaseType::ClickHouse and SQLDialect::ClickHouse with
  defaultPort=8123 (8443 when sslEnabled). Backtick-quoted identifiers.
* AdapterFactory routes to the new adapter.
* nlohmann/json FetchContent moves to the top-level CMakeLists so both
  Data and Services can link nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json without
  worrying about add_subdirectory ordering.
* Qt6::Network linked into gridex-data for the HTTP transport.

UI: no changes required — ConnectionForm iterates kAllDatabaseTypes so
ClickHouse appears in the type combo automatically with the generic
host/port/user/pass/db layout.

Verified locally against clickhouse/clickhouse-server:latest:
* Connect with default:test123 to localhost:8123, database `demo`.
* Sidebar lists `demo` schema with `events` (5 rows) and `users` (3 rows).
* SELECT JOIN across both tables returns expected rows with mixed types
  (LowCardinality, Nullable, Decimal, DateTime, Date, Bool, Uint*).
* ALTER TABLE … UPDATE/DELETE on MergeTree succeeds; the same on a Log
  engine table is rejected pre-flight with a clear message.

* JwtDecoder.{h,cpp} — payload decode for `exp` / `email` /
  `chatgpt_account_id` / `chatgpt_plan_type` (no signature verification —
  issuer is reached over TLS).
* OAuthLoopbackServer.{h,cpp} — single-shot QTcpServer bound to
  127.0.0.1:1455-1458 (ephemeral fallback), parses the GET callback,
  serves a Catppuccin-styled "you can close this tab" page, calls back
  with code+state. Times out after 180 s.
* ChatGPTOAuthService.{h,cpp} — orchestrates signIn / refresh / signOut /
  status. Persists the token bundle via SecretStore (libsecret). Auto-
  refresh request and refresh-token-rejected handling (wipes bundle on
  refresh_token_expired/reused/invalidated). Browser is opened via
  xdg-open through QProcess so the service library does not pull in
  Qt6::Gui.

LLM provider (Services/AI/Providers/ChatGPTProvider.{h,cpp}):
* Synchronous ILLMService using QEventLoop'd Qt Network calls — matches
  the existing AnthropicProvider pattern.
* In-process token refresh: load bundle from libsecret → if access_token
  is within kRefreshSkewSeconds of `exp`, POST /oauth/token with
  refresh_token blocking → persist rotated bundle → use new access_token.
* sendMessage() → POST chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses with the
  Codex-CLI wire format (instructions = system prompt; input = typed
  message items with input_text / output_text content parts;
  stream:true, store:false). Walks the SSE byte stream and accumulates
  `response.output_text.delta` payloads into a single string.
* availableModels() → GET /models?client_version=1.0.0 with the bearer
  + ChatGPT-Account-ID headers; filters to supported_in_api &&
  visibility==list to drop hidden / deprecated entries.
* 401/403 wipes the bundle and surfaces AuthenticationError so the UI
  prompts re-sign-in.

Storage (Data/Keychain/SecretStore.h):
* Adds save/load/delete helpers under the "ai.chatgpt.tokens.<key>"
  namespace, mirroring the existing API-key + DB-password conventions.

Models (Core/Models/AI/ChatGPTTokenBundle.h):
* Plain struct with toJson/fromJson — single source of truth for the
  serialized bundle layout (access/refresh/id token + decoded claims +
  obtainedAt epoch).

Wiring:
* AIServiceFactory routes "ChatGPT" to ChatGPTProvider.
* CMake adds the new sources to gridex-services.

UI (Settings → AI Providers):
* "ChatGPT" appears alongside Anthropic / OpenAI / Ollama / Gemini in
  the provider combo.
* Selecting it hides the API-key + custom-endpoint rows and shows an
  OAuth row with status pill ("Signed in as foo@bar.com (plus)") plus
  Sign in / Sign out buttons.
* Sign in opens the browser via xdg-open and waits on the loopback
  listener; on success the model dropdown auto-populates from
  /models. On failure the status pill turns red with the server message.
* QFormLayout-row visibility now flips through a captured aiForm_
  member — the previous attempt cast the wrong layer (page->layout()
  returned the outer QVBoxLayout, not the form), so the OAuth row
  never showed.

Polish:
* The 80×16 indeterminate QProgressBar next to the model combo is
  replaced with a 14-px Braille-glyph spinner (⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏) running
  at ~12 fps in the accent colour. Smaller, calmer, matches the rest
  of the UI's visual weight.

Verified end-to-end against a real ChatGPT Plus account: sign-in works,
the model list populates, the AI chat panel returns assistant responses,
and the bundle survives an app restart (loaded from libsecret).

fix(grid): re-introspect schema on Cmd+R and sidebar double-click (#63)

Cmd+R was calling `loadPage()` which re-fetched rows but never updated
`viewModel.columns`. When the table schema had changed externally
(e.g. someone ran ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN), the grid would render new
row data against the stale column list, shifting values into the wrong
columns or producing trailing NULLs.

Single-clicking an already-open table in the sidebar also did nothing —
`AppState.openTable` short-circuited to focus the existing tab without
any reload signal — so users had no visible way to refresh.

The view model already exposed `reloadAfterStructureChange()`, which
invalidates the static `metadataCache[cacheKey]` and runs a full
`load()` (rows + columns + PK + FK + enum metadata). Wire that into:

* DataGridView — Cmd+R handler and the discard-pending-changes path
  both call `reloadAfterStructureChange()` instead of `loadPage()`.
* SidebarView — added an `.onTapGesture(count: 2)` on table/view rows
  that focuses the tab and posts `.reloadData`. Single-click semantics
  are unchanged.

Workaround prior to this fix was to disconnect and reconnect the whole
connection.

fix(mcp): stub unimplemented capability handlers & auto-connect on stdio startup

The macOS MCP server advertises `prompts` and `resources` capabilities during
`initialize`, but the request dispatcher never handled `prompts/list`,
`resources/list`, or `resources/templates/list` — each fell through to the
default branch and returned `-32601 Method not found`. Strict MCP clients
(e.g. Claude Code) treat that as a fatal protocol violation and tear down the
stdio pipe immediately after init, so the full tool surface was unreachable
despite tools/list itself working.

Additionally, `runMCPServerAsync` constructed a fresh `ConnectionManager`,
registered MCP modes, and started the server without ever opening a single DB
connection. Because `--mcp-stdio` runs in a separate process from the GUI, no
live adapters are inherited, so any tool that goes through
`MCPToolContext.getAdapter` (`list_tables`, `query`, `get_sample_rows`, …)
returned `Connection '<uuid>' not found.` even though `list_connections`
happily reported the config.

Changes:
- MCPServer.swift: handle `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, and
  `resources/templates/list` with empty-array results; alias
  `notifications/initialized` with the legacy `initialized` notification name.
- main.swift: in stdio mode, instantiate a `KeychainService`, then for every
  non-locked connection, load its DB password (and SSH password if applicable)
  and call `connectionManager.connect(...)`. Failures are logged to stderr but
  do not block server startup.

Verified on macOS 15.7.5 (arm64) against PostgreSQL 16: full Claude Code MCP
handshake succeeds and `list_tables` / `list_schemas` / `query` execute
end-to-end against a live DB.
